title: Neighbourhood grants, water reports and Fergus cell tower
subtitle: Also: cannabis retail request, Fergus Scottish Festival update, two farm severance rezonings, land use planning workshop.
overview: The committee recommended continuing the Neighbourhood Grant program for 2023 under option 1 and asked staff to look at the program's future in the 2024 budget {{vote:m1}}. The program began as a 2022 pilot meant to bring neighbours together, and staff said it took considerable time to administer.

The committee also recommended that Council give municipal concurrence to a 22 m Bell Mobility monopole at 810 St. David Street North in Fergus {{vote:m3}}. The tower needs federal approval, so the Township's role is to support or not support it. It also received the 2022 water, wastewater and source protection annual reports for information {{vote:m2}}.

Delegations included a request that staff report on allowing private retail cannabis stores, and an update from the Fergus Scottish Festival. Two public meetings on farm surplus severance rezonings took place, and a planning workshop was held. After a closed session on a confidential commercial matter, the Deputy Mayor reported only that direction was given to staff.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended proceeding with option 1 for 2023 and directing staff to investigate the program's future in the 2024 Budget.

decisions.item: Telecommunication tower concurrence, 810 St. David Street North
decisions.detail: The committee recommended giving municipal concurrence to Bell Mobility's proposed 22 m monopole in Fergus and authorizing the Managing Director of Planning and Development to prepare the concurrence letter.
The committee received the 2022 drinking water, wastewater treatment plant and risk management official reports for information.

debate: On the Neighbourhood Grant, staff said the 2022 pilot drew many applications and needed a lot of staff time for street closures, police contact, barricades and insurance. Staff suggested a standard event kit to streamline this. One councillor favoured option 1 because the aim is neighbours gathering, not the dollar amount.

Staff said selecting grant recipients was hard because applications were very similar, so one event per area was chosen last year. Staff plan to fold the program into the community impact grant through the 2024 budget.

The cannabis delegates argued that residents must travel to other towns or rely on slow, costly delivery, and that regulated stores would reduce illegal sales. They cited a past Township survey and their own informal poll. Councillors asked about revenue for municipalities that opted in, and about youth access and store placement.

On the Bell tower, the delegate said the existing Fergus site is overloaded and that co-locating on the nearby tower was not workable. Councillors asked about helicopter safety and radio-frequency emissions. Staff said no public comments were received, and one councillor asked how the public is notified.

On the water reports, one councillor asked for future reports to show firm and operational capacity alongside approved capacity. Staff said they could provide this and described sewer relining and an infiltration study to reduce wastewater bypasses.
